continuity: Cheongpung intercepted the blood-red attack aimed at Jin Taekyung; after the blast breached Xining’s wall, Cheongpung could not be found.
The attackers breached Xining’s wall, and fighting continues at the breach.
The Blood Lord is approaching Jin Taekyung.
plot: Jin Taekyung cuts through the fanatics attacking Xining, entering a No-self Trance and nearing another insight. A blood-red attack breaks his trance; Cheongpung intercepts it, and the blast breaches the city wall.
Taekyung survives with no apparent serious injuries and returns to the fight, but Cheongpung is missing. Taekyung blames himself for pursuing enlightenment as the Blood Lord approaches.
translation_decisions: Keep No-self distinct from Trance: No-self is the self-forgetting state; Trance describes the intense dreamlike state Taekyung experiences.
Render 일기당천 as “One Against a Thousand.”

active_continuity: Dark Heaven and the Potala Palace are attacking Xining; the siege is underway.
The Blood Lord has coordinated pressure across the gates to exhaust the defenders and create an opening.
The Dalai Lama leads roughly ten thousand Potala Palace monks toward the North Gate to attack Jeok Cheongang and avenge the Palace’s ancestral grievance.
The Blood Lord expects allies to arrive by river from the east; a skeletal eagle signaled their approach.
Xining’s wall has been breached; fighting continues at the breach.
Cheongpung intercepted an attack aimed at Taekyung and is missing after the blast.
The Blood Lord is approaching Taekyung.
open_questions: Why does the Lord of Heaven want Taekyung, and what does he intend to do with him?
Whom do the Eldest Senior Brother and Elders serve, and what was Mu Song about to reveal?
Who are the allies approaching by river from the east?
Which of Cheongheoja’s Disciples is the hidden Dark Heaven agent, and what did Cheongheoja ask Taekyung to do?
What happened to Cheongpung after he intercepted the attack?
temporary_decisions: Render 西藏 as “Xizang” for the Murim region; retain “Tibet” when Taekyung identifies it from his modern-world perspective.
